With a WebSocket-only route registered through the internal hook of FR-HTTP-008 AC-7, a plain `GET` to that path is answered `426` with headers `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade` and, in wave 3, `Content-Length: 0`, asserted through the in-memory adapter. [D-395; T06; wave decision: 426 over TinyHttpd]

With the same WebSocket-only hook route, a `GET` carrying `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade` (for which the router returns a `MATCHED` result with route kind `WEBSOCKET`) is answered in wave 3 with the same `426`, both headers and `Content-Length: 0`, and no handshake is attempted, until wave 7 adds `app.ws`; this is the dispatcher mapping that FR-HTTP-008 AC-7 relies on. [D-395; T06; FR-ROUTE-015]

After `app.route(Method.any().except(Method.DELETE), "/t", h)`, `DELETE /t` through the in-memory harness is answered `405` with `Allow` = `GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, OPTIONS` (the router's `Method` declaration order, FR-ROUTE-010 AC-1) and `Content-Length: 0` in wave 3. [D-395] [T02]

records.requirement: The system shall answer the no-match result with `404`, the method-mismatch result with `405` and an `Allow` header, the automatic-OPTIONS result with `204` and an `Allow` header, the unsupported-method result with `501` and the WebSocket-only result with `426` plus `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade`, where in wave 3 (until wave 4 gives the error statuses the standard error body) the `400`, `404`, `405`, `426` and `501` answers carry an empty body with `Content-Length: 0`, and the `204` answers carry no body.
records.rationale: Covers D-395 (T02, T05, T06) and the wave decisions on automatic response bodies and `426` over TinyHttpd (the in-memory tests assert both `426` headers; the TinyHttpd gap is recorded in `carried-into-wave-7.md`, wave 7). Wave 4 gives the error statuses the standard error body.

records.title: Automatic HEAD through the GET handler

acceptanceCriteria.text: With only `GET /h` registered writing status `200`, header `X-A: 1` and body `hello`, `HEAD /h` through the harness is answered `200` with `X-A: 1` and no body bytes. [D-396; T05]
Inside the `GET` handler run for an automatic `HEAD`, `req.method()` returns `Method.HEAD`. [D-398; D-042; wave decision: req.method() during automatic HEAD]

records.requirement: The system shall, for an automatic-`HEAD` result, run the `GET` handler and send its status and headers without a body, with `req.method()` returning `HEAD` inside that handler.
records.rationale: Covers D-396 (T05), D-398 (the `req.method()` value) and the wave decision on `req.method()` during automatic `HEAD`; also D-042 (actual method reported).

records.title: Asterisk-form OPTIONS and raw paths not starting with a slash

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the in-memory adapter, `OPTIONS *` is answered `204` with `Allow` listing exactly the methods of `Method.any()` in `Method` declaration order and no body, even when no route is registered. [D-442; loop D: V1-006/V2-004]

`OPTIONS *` reaches neither the router lookup nor the path validator: with a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)`, `OPTIONS *` is still answered `204` with the `Allow` of AC-1 (not the validator's `400` for a raw path `*`), and `h` records no call. [D-442; D-052]
A raw path `abc` and a raw path `*` with method `GET` are each answered `400` with `Content-Length: 0` without route lookup. [D-442; wave decision: Automatic response bodies]
The `OPTIONS *` and non-`/` cases are tested through the in-memory adapter in wave 3; their TinyHttpd counterparts are not asserted in this requirement. [I-021; wave decision: Adapter halves]

records.requirement: The system shall answer the asterisk-form request `OPTIONS *` (raw path `*`) with `204` and an `Allow` header listing the methods of `Method.any()`, without route lookup or path validation, and answer any other raw path that does not start with `/` with `400`.
records.rationale: Covers D-442 and the loop D fix V1-006/V2-004 (I-021), on the in-memory adapter in wave 3; the TinyHttpd half of D-442 and I-021 is wave 5 work. D-036 defines `Method.any()`.

records.title: Interim handler failure and unfinished-response handling

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that throws `RuntimeException` before writing anything is answered `500` with an empty body through the harness. [wave decision: Interim failure handling]
A handler that throws a checked `IOException` after setting status `201` but before commit is answered `500` with an empty body. [wave decision: Interim failure handling]

A handler that throws after commit while the response is `STREAMING` (the only committed-but-incomplete state a wave 3 handler can reach) leaves the response `ABORTED` and the in-memory adapter reports the exchange closed abnormally instead of a `500`; a handler that throws after the response is `COMPLETED` (for example after `res.send("x")`) leaves it `COMPLETED`, because abort is a no-op there, with the sent bytes unchanged and no `500`. [D-097; D-099; wave decision: abort() after completion; wave decision: Interim failure handling]

A handler that sets `status(202)` and `header("X-A", "1")` and returns without a body write or `end()` yields `202` with `X-A: 1` and an empty body, and the response is `COMPLETED`. [wave decision: Interim failure handling]

records.requirement: The system shall, until wave 4 adds the error path, answer an exception thrown by a handler with `500` and an empty body while the response is not committed, abort the response when the exception is thrown after commit or while streaming, and finish a non-streaming response left unfinished by a returning handler with the status and headers set so far and an empty body.
records.rationale: Covers the wave decision on interim failure handling (D-126, D-127, D-129, D-134 replaced in wave 4; D-097, D-099, D-131).

records.title: One handler for a Method or MethodSet reports the actual method

acceptanceCriteria.text: After `app.route(Method.get().post().delete(), "/users/:id", h)`, `GET`, `POST` and `DELETE /users/1` through the harness all reach `h`, and `PUT /users/1` is answered `405`. [D-041; T01]
Inside `h`, `req.method()` returns `Method.GET`, `Method.POST` and `Method.DELETE` for those three requests respectively. [D-042; T01]
After `app.route(Method.PATCH, "/p", h)`, `PATCH /p` reaches `h` with `req.method()` = `Method.PATCH`. [D-041; D-042]
`HEAD /users/1` reaches `h` through automatic `HEAD` with `req.method()` = `Method.HEAD`. [D-042; wave decision: req.method() during automatic HEAD]

records.requirement: The system shall register the one handler given to `route(Method, path, handler)` or `route(MethodSet, path, handler)` for every method in the argument, and report the actual request method through `req.method()` when a request reaches that handler.
records.rationale: Covers D-041 and D-042 (T01) and the wave decision on `req.method()` during automatic `HEAD`.

records.title: Internal RestApp implementation with deferred router build and freeze

acceptanceCriteria.text: The implementation is a public class in a package documented as internal and not part of the API contract, it implements `RestApp`, and it holds the router and the dispatcher. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-393]
A registration with an invalid pattern (one that `RoutePattern.parse` rejects) throws at the registration call itself, before any freeze. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-047; D-048]

`app.get("/a/b", h)` followed by `app.routerPolicy(RouterPolicy.builder().mergeSlashes(true).build())` makes `GET /a//b` reach `h` after the harness freeze, showing the policy applies to registrations made before it. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; FR-ROUTE-006]

The `Router` is constructed only at the freeze, and a duplicate of D-044 surfaces as the freeze's `RoutingConfigException`, not at the second registration call. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-044]

After the harness freeze, `app.get(...)`, `app.route(Method, path, h)`, `app.route(MethodSet, path, h)` and `app.routerPolicy(...)` each throw `IllegalStateException`, and `RouteBuilder` registration methods (`get`, `put`, ...) throw `IllegalStateException` too, including on a builder obtained from `app.route(path)` before the freeze. [wave decision: Settings after the freeze]
No public static method or constructor in package `com.snoworca.naruserve` returns a `RestApp` in wave 3. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-111]

The internal implementation (not the public `RestApp` interface) offers an internal WebSocket-route registration hook that records a WebSocket registration and passes it to `Router.addWebSocket` at the freeze; the test-fixtures harness uses it to register a WebSocket-only route, and wave 3 dispatches no handshake to that route (a matching upgrade request gets the same `426` as a plain `GET`) until wave 7 adds `app.ws`. [D-395; T06; wave decision: Working app in wave 3]

records.requirement: The system shall provide in an internal package of `NaruServe-api` a `RestApp` implementation that holds the router and the dispatcher, parses each registered pattern at the registration call, records the registrations and the routing policy, builds the `Router` with that policy only at the route-table freeze, and rejects any registration or `routerPolicy` call after the freeze with `IllegalStateException`. Wave 3 adds no public factory for it.
records.rationale: Covers D-393 and D-044 (duplicate raised at freeze) and the wave decisions on the working app in wave 3 (D-047, D-048, D-058, D-111, D-154) and settings after the freeze (D-114, D-152). Wave 4 makes `listen()` run the same freeze and ties the after-freeze rule to the `NEW` state.

records.title: Request path, raw path and path parameter accessors

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `GET /files/a%20b?x=1` matched by `/files/:name`, `req.path()` returns `/files/a b`. [D-073]
For the same request `req.rawPath()` returns `/files/a%20b`, without `?x=1`. [D-074; wave decision: Remaining markers]
For the same request `req.param("name")` returns `a b`. [D-075]
`req.param("missing")` for a name not in the matched pattern throws an exception instead of returning `null`. [D-075]

traceLinks.notes: single percent-decoding of path and params

records.requirement: The system shall make `req.path()` return the decoded path without the query string, `req.rawPath()` return the raw, undecoded path without the query string, and `req.param(name)` return the decoded value of a variable of the matched pattern and throw an exception for a name absent from that pattern.
records.rationale: Covers D-073, D-074, D-075 and the wave decision on remaining markers (`rawPath()` excludes the query string, which stays available through `req.query(...)`).
records.implementationNotes:
- -
- [2026-10-19] req.path() for /a//b under mergeSlashes(true) (/a//b or /a/b) is not fixed by FR-ROUTE-006 or the design: left to implementer, C-07; the chosen value is recorded at close so wave 5 can compare adapters.

records.title: Query accessors with form-urlencoded decoding and malformed-query 400

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `?a=1&a=2&b=3`, `req.query("a")` returns `1`, `req.queries("a")` returns `[1, 2]`, `req.query("c")` returns `null` and `req.queries("c")` returns an empty list. [D-076; T07]
For `?q=a+b%20c&%ED%95%9C=%EA%B8%80`, `req.query("q")` returns `a b c` and `req.query("한")` returns `글`. [D-077; T07]

A query `?x=%zz`, a query `?x=%E0%A4` (truncated UTF-8) and a query `?x=%C3%28` (invalid UTF-8) are each answered `400` and the matched handler is not called. [D-078; T07; wave decision: Interim failure handling]

records.requirement: The system shall decode the raw query string as UTF-8 `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` text with `+` read as a space, make `req.query(name)` return the first value or `null` and `req.queries(name)` every value in request order or an empty list, and answer a query with malformed percent-encoding or invalid UTF-8 with `400` before the handler runs.
records.rationale: Covers D-076, D-077, D-078 (T07, in-memory part), the wave decision on interim failure handling (query decoded before the handler) and the residual on pre-request rejections (a malformed query is decoded after the `Request` exists, so D-117 and D-129 apply to it).
records.implementationNotes:
- -
- [2026-10-19] The malformed query is decoded after the `Request` exists, so wave 4 middleware and onError see that `400` (D-117, D-129); not observable in wave 3, hence no AC. [wave-3 residual: pre-request rejections]

records.title: Header, remote address, secure flag and Last-Event-ID accessors

acceptanceCriteria.text: With headers `X-Tag: a` and `x-tag: b`, `req.header("X-TAG")` returns `a`, `req.headers("x-Tag")` returns `[a, b]`, `req.header("None")` returns `null` and `req.headers("None")` returns an empty list. [D-079; T07]

With the in-memory adapter reporting remote address `10.0.0.5` and secure `false`, a request carrying `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4`, `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` and `Forwarded: for=1.2.3.4;proto=https` still yields `req.remoteAddress()` = `10.0.0.5` and `req.isSecure()` = `false`. [D-080]
`req.lastEventId()` returns `42` for header `Last-Event-ID: 42` and `null` when the header is absent. [D-081]

traceLinks.notes: remote address and secure flag from the SPI

records.requirement: The system shall make `req.header(name)` match names case-insensitively and return the first value or `null`, `req.headers(name)` return every value or an empty list, `req.remoteAddress()` and `req.isSecure()` report the adapter's values while ignoring `X-Forwarded-*` and `Forwarded` headers, and `req.lastEventId()` return the `Last-Event-ID` header value or `null`.
records.rationale: Covers D-079 (T07), D-080 and D-081. The proxy-trust configuration API of D-080 belongs to #8 and does not exist in wave 3, so proxy headers are always ignored here.

records.title: Per-request concurrent attribute store

acceptanceCriteria.text: After `req.attribute("user", u)`, `req.attribute("user", User.class)` returns `u`, and `req.attribute("none", User.class)` returns `null`. [D-082]
An attribute stored while handling one request is not visible through `attribute(key, type)` of a second request, including two requests handled concurrently. [D-082]
Eight threads writing distinct keys to the same request's attributes concurrently leave every key readable with its value and no exception. [D-083]

With a typed `null` variable `Object v = null`, `req.attribute("k", v)` removes `k`, so a later `req.attribute("k", Object.class)` returns `null`; the value parameter is annotated `@Nullable`. [wave decision: Null attribute values; D-072]
`req.attribute("k", Integer.class)` with a stored `String` throws `ClassCastException`. [wave decision: Remaining markers]

records.requirement: The system shall store request attributes per request in a concurrent map that never holds `null`, where `req.attribute(key, value)` stores a value or removes the key when the value is `null`, and `req.attribute(key, type)` returns the value, `null` for a missing key, or throws `ClassCastException` when the stored value is not of `type`.
records.rationale: Covers D-082, D-083 and the wave decisions on null attribute values and remaining markers (`ClassCastException` on a type mismatch). D-072 makes the value parameter `@Nullable`.

records.title: Response chaining and default status

acceptanceCriteria.text: `res.status(201)` and `res.header("X-A", "1")` each return the same `Response` instance they were called on, so `res.status(201).header("X-A", "1").send("ok")` yields `201` with `X-A: 1`. [D-089]
A handler that calls only `res.send("ok")` yields status `200`. [D-090]

records.requirement: The system shall make `res.status` and `res.header` return the same `Response` for chaining, a rule that `res.addCookie` and `res.cache` follow once waves 5 and 6 add them, and default a response to status `200`.
records.rationale: Covers D-089 and D-090 and the wave decision on the request and response surface (`addCookie` and `cache` are not added in wave 3).

records.title: Response body writers send, html, stream and end

acceptanceCriteria.text: `res.send("hé")` writes the UTF-8 bytes `68 C3 A9` with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8`, and after `res.header("Content-Type", "text/csv")` it keeps `text/csv`. [D-091]

`res.html("

é

")` writes UTF-8 bytes with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8`. [D-092]

`res.send(new byte[]{0, (byte) 0xFF, 10})` writes exactly those three bytes with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` when none was set, and keeps an explicitly set `Content-Type`. [D-093; wave decision: Remaining markers]

`res.stream(in, "application/pdf")` with a 1 MiB input writes all bytes in order with `Content-Type: application/pdf`, and a counting input stream shows that every `read(byte[], int, int)` call requests fewer bytes than the 1 MiB input. [D-094]

`res.stream(...)` closes the input stream exactly once after a successful copy, after a read failure, and after `res.abort(...)` during the transfer, including when the handler already returned; the caller does not close it. [D-094; wave decision: stream() closing]
`res.end()` completes the response with the status and headers set so far and no body. [D-095]

`res.stream(InputStream, contentType)` does not block until the copy ends: it commits the response and returns, the copy to the end of the stream runs after the handler returns, and the response is `STREAMING` until the copy ends; a test whose handler returns right after `res.stream(...)` observes the call return before the input is read to its end. [D-094; D-103; wave decision: stream() closing]

records.requirement: The system shall make `res.send(String)` write UTF-8 text with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8` unless a `Content-Type` was set, `res.html(String)` write UTF-8 text with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8`, `res.send(byte[])` write the bytes unchanged with `application/octet-stream` when no `Content-Type` was set, `res.stream(InputStream, contentType)` copy the stream to its end in bounded chunks while taking ownership of the stream and closing it when the transfer ends by success, failure or abort, and `res.end()` complete the response without a body.
records.rationale: Covers D-091, D-092, D-093, D-094, D-095 and the wave decisions on `stream()` closing (W2-007) and remaining markers (`application/octet-stream` default, as Express does for a `Buffer`). No chunk size is fixed here.

records.title: Response commit flag, abort and header CR/LF rejection

acceptanceCriteria.text: `res.isCommitted()` is `false` before any body write and `true` after `res.send("x")` handed the status and headers to the in-memory adapter. [D-096]
`res.abort(new IOException("x"))` during a `stream(...)` transfer makes the in-memory adapter report the connection closed abnormally and leaves the response state `ABORTED`. [D-097]

`res.abort(...)` on a response that is already `COMPLETED` or `ABORTED` does nothing: no exception, the state is unchanged and the adapter sees no further close. [wave decision: abort() after completion]
`res.header("X\r\nY", "1")`, `res.header("X", "a\nb")` and `res.header("X", "a\rb")` each throw an exception and add no header. [D-098]

records.requirement: The system shall make `res.isCommitted()` return `true` once the status line and headers were handed to the transport, make `res.abort(error)` end the response abnormally by closing the connection and set the state to `ABORTED`, and make `res.header(name, value)` reject a name or value containing CR or LF with an exception.
records.rationale: Covers D-096, D-097, D-098 and the wave decision on `abort()` after completion (no-op on a complete or aborted response).

records.title: Response state machine with single commit

acceptanceCriteria.text: A response starts in `NEW`, is `COMMITTED` once status and headers are handed to the adapter, and reaches `COMPLETED` after `send`; the adapter receives the status line and headers exactly once. [D-099]
`res.status(500)` or `res.header("X", "1")` after `res.send("a")` committed the response throws an exception and the sent status and headers stay unchanged. [D-100]
A second body call (`send`, `html`, `stream` or `end`) after a body was sent throws an exception and writes no further bytes. [D-101]

After `res.stream(...)` returns, the response is `STREAMING` until the copy ends, then `COMPLETED`, or `ABORTED` on abort; a read failure of the input stream during the copy, including after the handler returned, ends the response `ABORTED` with the input stream closed (FR-HTTP-014 AC-5). [D-103; D-097; wave decision: stream() closing]

While the response is `STREAMING` (committed but not completed), `res.status(500)` and `res.header("X", "1")` each throw an exception and the status and headers the adapter received stay unchanged. [D-100; D-099]

records.requirement: The system shall move each response through the states `NEW`, `COMMITTED`, `STREAMING`, `COMPLETED` and `ABORTED`, committing at most once, throw an exception for `status` or `header` after commit and for a second body after a body was sent, and keep a streaming response in `STREAMING` after the handler returns until the transfer ends.
records.rationale: Covers D-099, D-100, D-101 and D-103 and the wave decision on `stream()` closing. D-100 applies to `addCookie` and `cache` once waves 5 and 6 add them; among the streaming responses only `stream` exists in wave 3.

records.title: Bodyless 204, 304 and HEAD responses

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that calls `res.status(204).send("x")` yields `204` with zero body bytes through the in-memory adapter. [D-102]
A handler that calls `res.status(304).send(new byte[]{1, 2})` yields `304` with zero body bytes. [D-102]
An explicit `HEAD /h` route whose handler calls `res.send("body")` yields its status and headers with zero body bytes. [D-102]
The automatic `204` answers of `OPTIONS` and `OPTIONS *` carry zero body bytes. [D-102; wave decision: Automatic response bodies]

records.requirement: The system shall send responses with status `204` or `304`, and every response to a `HEAD` request, without a message body, discarding any body the handler supplied.
records.rationale: Covers D-102 and the wave decision on automatic response bodies (`204` replies carry no body). Used by automatic `HEAD` (D-396).

records.title: Mutation after completion throws while read accessors stay usable

acceptanceCriteria.text: After `res.send("a")` completed the response, `res.status(201)`, `res.header("X", "1")`, `res.send("b")`, `res.html("c")`, `res.send(new byte[0])`, `res.stream(in, "text/plain")` and `res.end()` each throw `IllegalStateException`. [D-084]
After completion, `req.path()`, `req.query("q")`, `req.header("H")`, `req.attribute("k", Object.class)` and `res.isCommitted()` return their values without exception. [D-084]
After completion, `res.abort(...)` returns without exception and changes nothing. [D-084; wave decision: abort() after completion]

records.requirement: The system shall throw `IllegalStateException` for a mutating `Response` call (`status`, `header` or a body write) after the response completed, a rule that `addCookie` and `cache` follow from waves 5 and 6, while the read accessors of `Request` and `Response`, `isCommitted()` and `abort()` stay usable after completion.
records.rationale: Covers D-084 and the wave decisions on the request and response surface (`addCookie` and `cache` from waves 5 and 6) and `abort()` after completion. Middleware and `onError` arrive in wave 4; wave 3 checks the rule from code that runs after the handler finished the response.

records.title: Request body ownership with BodyState and BodyAlreadyConsumedException

acceptanceCriteria.text: `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` is a public class in `com.snoworca.naruserve` extending `RuntimeException`. [D-086; wave decision: Body ownership]

`BodyState` is an internal class whose state is `UNREAD` initially, `PARSING` while a reader holds the body, and `CONSUMED` after a completed read or `CLOSED` after the body was closed; a unit test drives each transition. [D-085]

A unit test acquiring the body through `BodyState` after a first read gets `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` when the second read is of a different kind (JSON, form/multipart or raw) or is a second JSON or raw read; the shared form/multipart parse of AC-4 is the only exemption. [D-086]

A unit test acquiring the shared form/multipart parse through `BodyState` repeatedly gets the same parse result each time without a second read of the stream and without `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`. [D-087]
A reflection test finds no public body-reading method on `Request` at the wave 3 merge (wave 5 adds the body readers). [wave decision: Body ownership]

records.requirement: The system shall track each request body with an internal `BodyState` moving from `UNREAD` through `PARSING` to `CONSUMED` or `CLOSED`, throw the public unchecked `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` of package `com.snoworca.naruserve` for any body read after the first one, and let repeated `form`, `file`, `files` and `parts` reads share one parse as the only exemption. Wave 3 exposes no public body-reading method.
records.rationale: Covers D-085, D-086, D-087 and the wave decision on body ownership (W2-004; I-012). The JSON, form, multipart and raw readers arrive in waves 5 and 6, so wave 3 tests these rules through `BodyState` directly; the raw kind is an internal consumer of the body stream.

records.title: Limit-enforcing request body input stream

acceptanceCriteria.text: The stream is constructed from the source stream, a limit and an optional declared `Content-Length`; constructing it with limit `0` or a negative limit throws `IllegalArgumentException`. [D-088; wave decision: Body ownership]
With limit `10`, reading a 10-byte source returns all 10 bytes and end of stream without error. [D-088]

With limit `10`, reading an 11-byte source without a declared `Content-Length` (a chunked-style source of unknown length) throws the internal over-limit `IOException` subclass (a type distinct from plain `IOException`, named by the implementer) on the read that would return byte 11, and no byte beyond the limit is returned. [D-088]

With limit `10` and a declared `Content-Length` of `11`, the first read throws the same internal over-limit `IOException` subclass without reading any byte from the source, so the waves that add body readers can tell it from a transport `IOException` and answer `413`. [D-088]

records.requirement: The system shall provide an internal limit-enforcing input stream that requires a positive limit at construction and fails a read as soon as the bytes read from the incoming stream exceed that limit, whether or not the request carries `Content-Length`, so body size limits are enforced before and during parsing.
records.rationale: Covers D-088 and the wave decision on body ownership (positive limit required, no unlimited default; I-012). The HTTP-level `413` checks land with the body readers in waves 5 and 6; wave 3 tests the stream directly. No default limit value is set here.

records.title: Method.any() excludes TRACE and CONNECT

acceptanceCriteria.text: `Method.any()` contains exactly `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS` and contains neither `TRACE` nor `CONNECT`. [D-036]
`Method.any().except(Method.DELETE)` equals `Method.of(Method.GET, Method.HEAD, Method.POST, Method.PUT, Method.PATCH, Method.OPTIONS)`. [D-037]

`Method.any()` returns the same members when a router has `TRACE` and `CONNECT` routing enabled; `TRACE` or `CONNECT` enters a `MethodSet` only when named, as in `Method.of(Method.TRACE)`. [wave decision: TRACE/CONNECT policy]
